data: Amazing game with a great soundtrack and gameplay
Very good game, a lot of replay value
I highly recommend this game, as it is enjoyable and challenging,
Overall, very fun little game, with really nice graphics and soundtrack
An excellent turn based strategy game with a fun story line and great 8-bit graphics and audio
Keeps on crashing no matter what really tried to fix the problem and play the game
the gameplay is just irritating and frustrating

An interesting and challenging turn based strategy game.

You're a time travelling mech pilot who kills giant bugs to save planet earth, what more do I need to say?

A wonderful strategy game that always brings something new to the table. I've never had the same gameplay twice. My only con is that the game can be tricky. Even then, that is usually a good thing, in this game's case.
Very addicting gameplay loop, one of the most engaging turn based games I've ever played.

- interesting turn-based strategy game play
- many weapon types and upgrades
- many enemy types
- tons of mech types for replay value and challenges
- hot keys for most moves
- it is getting quite interesting and challenging after understanding core game mechanics
- nice soundtrack for different level

- not much tutorial (how to play) and information (how battle works and how various attacks works), or the tutorial was just bugged after I closed game few years ago
- have to learn the basic game mechanics by testing in playing
- game actually is quite hard (conquer first island) even I choose normal difficulty
- sometimes player can't do anything in certain situations
- it is really frustrating when game is just over (have to restart from first level) after one wrong step
- it is getting more annoying combine with lots of random factors (environment, enemy, object layout)
- no option for save/load scum like me lol

6.9/10
(
- interesting at start, getting more frustrating more playing, but I do have some fun moments
- if you just start this game, I recommend you to choose easy mode at first for better learning and gaming experience
)

ITB is amazing. It's design is simple to learn but hard to master. The art and music are great and really sell the atmosphere.

Even if you are not a fan of tactics games, on easy mode the game plays a lot like a puzzle game and I often play it to relax or destress.

If you're looking for a challenge, hard IS hard and the achievements system adds a decent amount of replayability. You will easily get more than 20+ hours of content from this alone!

ITB makes me feel smart and I like that.
Very rapid scaling in difficulty through levels makes it easy to adapt gameplay to the mood I'm in

I have avoided playing this game for years because it felt really complicated to play.
To be fair, I should have started way earlier because this game is short and it's great and the units are very easy to learn.
Overall I think I would give this game a solid 8-9 out of 10 and it is definitely a puzzle game master piece.

Highly recommended for those that are looking for a challenge or trying to find a short and fun game to play on the go.

Worth the cost if you're looking for a fun and challenging strategy/puzzle game. It's sandbox and somewhat non-linear approach gives you an opportunity to play this game however long you want or whichever direction you want.

Enjoy watching as the smallest of errors steam rolls into an impossible quagmire with each problem compounding the other to quickly make victory impossible. Know that since the game provides perfect knowledge of everything your enemy will do, it's entirely your fault that you didn't push that enemy slightly to one side rather than the other three moves back, thereby allowing a cavalcade of enemies to overwelm your crew. Wallow in frustration when you craft a perfect plan to trounce a seemingly impossible situation only to overlook or accidentally open an enemy sight-line or fail to calculate damage to include the extra explosion granted on death by an enemy psion, causing you to lose a mech or building unexpectedly and allowing the enemy free reign across the board.

Overall, a wonderfully addictive little puzzle game that punishes you so viciously, so completely, and so unfalteringly for any tiny mistake that it regularly makes you despair that its developers were ever born.

10/10
Simply the gold standard for isometric turn based strategy games. An instant classic. Bonus points for running on my 8 year old MacBook too.

An addictive isometric roguelike with giant mechs and insectoids. Losing bars on your power grid (which is basically your life bar) is a big feature of this game and it's more about how you recoup the losses rather than prevent them. My best runs have been those that I've managed to prevent as many power grid losses as possible or those where I had very minimal losses and pushed through to recoup them later in the run. You can definitely get predetermined "bad runs" where you lose a lot of power early on due to unpreventable RNG but the rest of the game is fun regardless.

My nomination for the “Most Fun with a Machine” award in the 2018 Steam Awards.

Faster paced strategy combat. Having apx. 5 turns per map in various, tightly knit combat events is very effective at keeping the game fun as well as having all of your decisions matter as a player. Solid variety of moves and character ability pools as well. The item and description lists are not encyclopedic by any means, but if you liked Advance Wars or Unicorn Overlord, grab this! Especially if you see it on sale. 

The value is very much here at its full price (I bought it a little under $20 USD).
It's pretty much like chess if chess was a completely different game than it is
If you like roguelikes, go for it. If you don't, then you'll probably wish the game had a level designer. 4/10.
You like chess? This game is chess deluxe version. Definitely worth playing (even if you feel too stupid for that - like me).
Very fun strategy game! I love the achievements for this game, but did wish there were harder ones for playing on harder difficulties!

this is the best strategy game ever and im obsessed with it and i like it more than ftl
good art cool story
i just wish there was more of it

If you like turn-based RPGs, this game's definitely worth your time. It starts out simple enough, but with time, it gets more complex, offering you more ways to play. The option to choose different teams of mechs is great. Which team you take can completely change the way you play the game. All in all, good stuff.

I don't usually like Roguelikes, and I don't normally gravitate to strategy games, but this one is really fun. Low skill floor and high skill celling, and it makes you actually care about the story on each subsequent loop, which is the big issue with most roguelikes for me. also a little bit of chess dna in the gameplay. highly recommend

If you like Faster Than Light , you will like Into the Breach . Both games have similar mechanics and the same idea - if you beat the game, try again with a different team. Doesn't forgive mistakes, requires care and logic. I recommend at least getting to know such a wonderful game, especially since the price is not great by the standards of 2021.
Game is dumb. kill all enemies and no more moves, lol the world gets a turn just to kill your mechs you spent hours playing with
Really fun game! I have lost many an evening to playing this game. So easy to lose yourself in. It's a very challenging game that is very simple to play but difficult to master!

Walks the line between very satisfying and deeply frustrating. The map making algorithm sometimes completely snookers you and makes some of your units unusable. Many of the units are completely useless regardless of the map. But there's achievements linked to using them, so if you're after all the achievements be prepared to wade through a tedious RNG lottery to get them. Often you'll be going through a perfect game and one of the maps on the last two islands will just make it impossible to win. But if you're using the good units its a really fun game.

A masterpiece in design and conceptualization and a very thought-through strategy game. Explore over a dozen brilliant mech squads and test your strategic thinking on a whole new level. The new update also brings tons of new content, adding squads, missions, enemies, and abilities. One of the best strategy games for an astoundingly low price! If you have Steam credit just lying around, this is the game to buy!

10 / 10

Finding interesting non-intuitive solutions for seemingly hopeless situations feeds my superiority complex.

On the other hand, overlooking obvious unwanted consequences of my poor decisions in the simplest of problems makes me feel dumb as nails.

Into The Breach is a fine puzzle game that proves that FTL wasn't a fluke. Everything from visuals to audio to mechanics are well thought out and polished. At times it's almost magical how the game arranges events where your squad can get out of a sticky situation with just the right combination of moves and abilities only to arrive into another different sticky situation where you can again get away with some more thinking and so on.

The only real weakness the game has is a lack of depth in gameplay that doesn't make it last long enough to make you really want to chase after every unlockable thing since access to squads is tied to your achievements, some of which require quite a bit of grind to nail due to RNG elements in the game.

If you're looking for the next FTL then this isn't it, but it's definitely a good game for anyone looking for a puzzle game disguised as monster mashing.

I wish I could give it a neutral review instead of positive or negative. I love the turn based tactics, but I don't love the "basic-ness" of the gameplay loop. I don't necessarily mind the roguelike loop of starting over and getting coins, keeping pilots, etc. I just wish there was deeper elements of the gameplay. Whether the weapons, the mechs, the vek, etc. It just feels really shallow with a basic "dont let bugs hit these buildings". End point. I mean its great for the price I paid and I like the pixel art, but it's hard to stay engaged with this game for more than 15-20 minutes at a time.
Makes you feel like a genius only for your enormous brain to realize the next turn that you could have done it better.

Has anyone compared this game to 4D chess yet? No? Well, it's bloody brilliant.

Anyway, to pile on to the chess analogy, this game is more like a chess study than a chess match: you're given slightly different objectives each time and just 5 turns to complete them or fail miserably. This makes for some intense situations with a lot of moving parts, which are really fun to "solve" or at least attempt to minimize the damage. There's a decent variety of mechs/pilots/weapons to master, as well as enemies and objectives to complete.

It's also really polished and "crisp" in terms of graphics, audio, and general gameplay, and loads really fast - ideal when you need a quick fix. Well, quick if you can force yourself to quit, of course.

PS. Advanced Edition rocks!

Into the Breach achieves something I thought was impossible by making turn-based combat exciting. Each scenario is about defeat waves of giant bugs while at the same time defending the civilian buildings which are caught in the crossfire. Every turn the game will put you into a desperate checkmate scenario where your options seem limited and it's on you to come up with a clever way to turn the tide and stay one step ahead. Unlike many tactical games there is almost zero ambiguity about what the enemy is going to do and what they are capable of. Into the Breach communicates so effectively to the player who is attacking what and when and what the consequences of that attack are, giving you more than enough information to make strategic decisions consistently. You can trick bugs into attacking each other, knock em into a landmine, bust open a dam and wash em away, there's so many badass stunts to pull off and they always feel earned.
spaghetti and meatballs.

ITB wasn't an instant 'thumb up' game for me. I tried to play it few times and didn't enjoy it. Then, I tried it again after some time and beat it in a few sessions. It's a good game with non-linear learning curve where you have to gradually unlock and find out the strategy that fits you best.

Lots of close battles that can easily end your run. Fast enough to restart that it doesn't matter. I can see this replacing Slay the Spire and FTL as my go-to game on the side. There's definitely room to try out plenty of strats and the maps are varied enough to keep it interesting.

Into the Breach is a turn-based game about fighting giant bugs with mechs. Oh, and since it was made by the same people as FTL, it's going to bloody difficult.

The game itself can feel frustrating, as failing one level can totally destroy the run, and therefore make you have to restart the entire campaign. And with the difficulty scale of each level, it's almost impossible to not restart a few times before you finally beat the game.

Each mechanic introduced into the game is designed to be used. Pushing, pulling, damage, water, and the abilities of the mechs all play major roles in the game. It is only after you play enough that you start to fully utilize each of these abilities of the different mechs.

In the beginning, it would seem some levels are impossible. You say "It's not possible! How do I stop them?" But as you play more and more, you are able to find the right combinations that allow you to get by the level by the skin of your teeth. And these moments are the most rewarding in the game Into the Breach.

Plus the music's pretty cool.
It's like if Pacific Rim was a game. I love the theme and how every round feels like a puzzle.
Both Into the Breach and FTL are great games, simple yet hard, have depth in it and decent replayability. Best wishes to devs!

One of, if not the best, puzzle strategy experiences out there. Even on lower difficulties, the game will require you to know your mechs, pilots, weapons and enemies near perfectly in order to beat a level optimally. An ideal set of moves to save everyone and complete all objectives sometimes won't exist, which can be a bit frustrating, but such situations are often a result of prior mistakes rather than an unfair game design. On the opposite end, figuring out a complicated set of moves to perfectly execute a turn is an instant hit of dopamine, and where this game shines the most.

The story, art style and soundtrack are simple, but charming. The gameplay is what you are here for, and everything else is designed to make room for that part of the experience, which is no way a bad thing.

Achievements being a progression mechanic is an an amazing idea. It was a blast getting all of them, and I wish more games would play around with a similar system.
Easily one of the greatest indie games ever made, together with FTL from the same developer. Looking forward for the next banger from them to sink time into!

Amazing. Really has to be one of my favourite games. Wasn't as brutally hard as I was expecting. I finished it the whole way on the first playthrough. But I really took my time each turn to make sure I made the perfect move. Which is what is so great about this game. Each turn, there appears to be an almost perfect move you can make. If you lose, it is not because of luck, but 100% because of poor tactics and/or a lack of patience. It is punishing if you make a mistake because a single poor move can be devestating. Looking forward to doing my 2nd playthrough on hard. (I did the first on normal)

Seriously a great game. Visuals, music, story, game design. Top notch.

I play games for 40 years, I just can tell that this game is exceptionnal : don't waste time, never boring, very challenging (I always play games at hard level) but not impossible, nice graphics and sound, cool upgrades, and a little luck but that not spoils the game. I come again and again now to win in hard mode with every team.
Can be tough at times but makes you feel like a tactical genius when you come up with a good strat.

A simple concept, but an infinite set of possibilities. In Into the Breach, you're given 3 mechs to fend off enemies for 5 turns on an 8x8 tile board. With each mech having its own moves, and 10 different trios of mechs to choose for each playthrough, you come across situations that force you to think outside of the box and make combos and plays to stop enemies from attacking your buildings+mechs, and if you're lucky, you can get them to attack each other. While it might not be as hard as Subset's other game FTL, it certainly involves a lot more thinking, and the turn-based structure allows you to walk away for a bit if you're stuck, and come back for a fresh look at the board, like chess. Pretty awesome roguelike strategy game, and the music+art are beautiful as well.

This game has en enormous tactical depth stemming from surprisingly simple mechanics! The variety of the cute little mech's abilities is astonishing. The UI is super well designed, clean and clear in showing all relevant detail in dialogues and on the map. I especially like the various features to increase UI and font size. Playing this game is very relaxing due to it's turn based nature and the fact that it can be controlled entirely using the mouse in one hand (and holding a cold beer in the other). Though playing with fully configurable hotkeys or a controller also works very well. Collecting the interestingly categorized achievements is especially fun, aided by ingame progress tracking and even necessary to unlock new squads. The satisfaction obtained from pulling off a genius combo that finishes multiple enemies at once keeps feeding the playing loop!

A gem of a game, every aspect is perfectly developed. Every gameplay choice is impactful, the setting is engrossing without wasteful exposition, the visual design is evocative while also being functional, and the soundtrack is excellent. Absolutely zero cruft, it's entirely difficult (but fun) decisions that create an engaging experience over and over again.

I've also played this on Switch so a lower playtime here. This game is the spirit and soul of turn based strategy distilled to its core. It's a deceptively simple, endlessly deep puzzle, and honestly a masterpiece in the genre.
Much like FTL this game is a good combo of hard in game fights and easy restarts. If you enjoy difficult Rouge-like games than this has got to be at the top of the list.

Best turn-based strategy game IMO. This game repeatedly puts you in a situation where you have more enemies than friendly units, forcing you to use your abilities creatively and strategically to survive against the odds. Everything that will happen in a turn, from enemy attacks, environmental damage, and even the consequences of your own actions, is illustrated from the start of every turn. This means you are not at the mercy of RNG which is great but also means you have no-one to blame but yourself when something unexpected happened. My Steam hours are not reflective of my actual hours played.
W game. Not too hard not too easy, perfect for when you dont want to have to lock in but also want to keep your brain running. Control Mech OP.

It's a puzzle game, which wasn't made clear in any way. By saying "from the makers of FTL" that kind of implies some kind of depth and comparison to FTL. Except this isn't a launch off of FTL that adds more to the concept. Instead it feels like a much more watered down version. Where FTL stood as an ocean in both width and depth, this is like a photo of that, a pool of the same water. Basically the same mechanics just watered down and degraded.

While this game is well made in many ways and functions well, it doesn't feel right. There's never more than "survive 4 turns" with increasingly unfair enemies that spawn every turn. Much like FTL, I wouldn't be suprised if this game was unbeatable without remarkably fortunate RNG

It's amazing, truly!

You DO like big, juicy robots, don't you? And there's all kinds of them!
The rules are simple: defeat the moths and spiders and the corporate islands will thank you by making your jougernots even cooler.

This game holds a special place in my pneumatic heart and I'm sure it will also in yours.
Precisely crafted turn-based combat game, with absolutely no bloat or unnecessary elements. Simple to learn how to play but with a very high skill ceiling.

tldr.text: Very Positive (94%): players love the gameplay and combat.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, with a few players also finding the gameplay frustrating.
